_doc: PSEUDOPOTENTIAL SETS (doc/CalcNetworkReview.md section 4, D-STRUCTDATA step 2, ruled 2026-10-02/2026-10-29).  One entry = a NAME a material
(materials.json `pp`) or a deck can refer to, and for each element in it the pseudopotential VARIANT: `valence` = q, the number of
valence electrons the GTH entry keeps (Zion), a key into gth_potentials.json for the entry's `functional`.  PP data is a property of
(element, pseudopotential), NOT of the material: q7 vs q15 Mn is the same crystal.  The ONE reader is qchem.Pseudopotential.Set;
everyone else is handed the value.  A pseudopotential is generated for a specific functional, so the set names it.
THE RULE (2026-11-11, OpenWork §3 'A deck cannot name Te with a PP'): an element with no `valence` entry resolves to the SMALLEST q the
GTH database (gth_potentials.json, generated from BasisSetData/GTH_POTENTIALS.txt) holds at the set's functional, so every element the
database covers resolves.  `valence` lists only the EXCEPTIONS to that rule (none in gth-lda-valence today: its old 18-element list
was the rule written out by hand, and every element it lacked, Te for one, was refused).

gth-lda-valence.comment: The smallest-q (valence-only, largest core) GTH-LDA entry of every element: the recipe every banked anchor was run at.
